enonce_markdown: Which event produces the first heart sound ("lub")?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The two heart sounds are caused by valves closing: the atrioventricular valves at the start of ventricular systole, and the semilunar valves at the start of diastole.

### Solution

At the start of ventricular systole the ventricular pressure rises above the atrial pressure and the **atrioventricular (bicuspid and tricuspid) valves close**; this is the first sound. The closing of the semilunar valves is the second sound. Answer: **c**.

enonce_markdown: A resting person has a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. What is the duration of one cardiac cycle?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Duration of one cycle (s) = 60 s divided by the number of beats per minute.

### Solution

Duration = $60 / 80 = 0.75$ s. Dividing 80 by 60 (1.33) is the usual error. Answer: **b**.

enonce_markdown: At one moment in the cardiac cycle the pressure in the left atrium is 0.8 kPa, in the left ventricle 13.0 kPa and in the aorta 10.5 kPa. What is the state of the valves?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A valve opens when the pressure behind it is higher than the pressure in front of it, and closes when the pressure behind falls below.

### Solution

Ventricular pressure (13.0 kPa) is much higher than atrial pressure (0.8 kPa), so the **atrioventricular valve is closed**. It is also higher than aortic pressure (10.5 kPa), so the **semilunar valve is open** and blood is ejected into the aorta. Answer: **d**.

choix.texte: Atrioventricular valve open, semilunar valve closed
Atrioventricular valve closed, semilunar valve open

enonce_markdown:
Pressures (kPa) in the left side of the heart were recorded at four times in one cycle.

| Time (s) | Left atrium | Left ventricle | Aorta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 1.2 | 0.9 | 10.7 |
| 0.15 | 0.9 | 6.0 | 10.5 |
| 0.25 | 1.5 | 15.8 | 15.5 |
| 0.35 | 1.4 | 9.0 | 11.0 |

For each time, state whether the atrioventricular (AV) valve and the semilunar valve are open or closed, and name the phase.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the ventricle with the atrium (AV valve) and the ventricle with the aorta (semilunar valve): the valve opens only if the pressure behind it is greater.

### Solution

| Time | AV valve | Semilunar valve | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 s | open (atrium 1.2 > ventricle 0.9) | closed (ventricle 0.9 < aorta 10.7) | atrial systole |
| 0.15 s | closed (ventricle 6.0 > atrium 0.9) | closed (ventricle 6.0 < aorta 10.5) | isovolumetric contraction, early ventricular systole |
| 0.25 s | closed | open (ventricle 15.8 > aorta 15.5) | ventricular ejection |
| 0.35 s | closed (ventricle 9.0 > atrium 1.4) | closed (ventricle 9.0 < aorta 11.0) | isovolumetric relaxation at the start of diastole |

enonce_markdown: What is the main function of the delay of about 0.1 s that the atrioventricular node imposes on the wave of excitation?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The cardiac cycle is a sequence: atria first, then ventricles. The structures that conduct the impulse set the timing.

### Solution

The delay lets the atria **finish contracting and emptying into the ventricles** before the ventricles begin to contract. Without it the atrioventricular valves would close before the ventricles were filled. The semilunar valves close later because of pressure, and rate is set by the sinoatrial node. Answer: **a**.

choix.texte: It allows the atria to finish emptying into the ventricles before ventricular systole
It allows the semilunar valves to close before the ventricles relax
It gives the sinoatrial node time to recover before it fires again
It speeds up the spread of excitation to the apex

enonce_markdown: In a patient with complete heart block, no impulse can pass from the atria to the ventricles. Which result is expected?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The heart is myogenic and every part of the conducting tissue can generate its own rhythm, but the fastest pacemaker (the sinoatrial node) normally sets the rate for all.

### Solution

The sinoatrial node still makes the atria contract at the normal rate. The ventricles no longer receive impulses from it, so they beat at their own slower intrinsic rhythm, independently of the atria. The ventricles are not stopped because the beat is myogenic, and it is not a delayed copy of the atrial rate since no impulse passes. Answer: **c**.

choix.texte: The ventricles contract at the atrial rate but 0.1 s later
The ventricles contract at a slower rate, independent of the atria
The heart stops because a heart without nerve impulses cannot beat
